sentences.text: The occurrence of the accident is not in dispute.
2. As a result of the accident, Sri.Parthasarathi, a 31 year old was killed.

3. In a claim petition filed by the wife, children and his parents, the Tribunal proceeded to award a sum of Rs.7,56,000/- along with the interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
4.
However, the Tribunal fastened the liability on the owner of the bus, since the bus did not have a permit to ply on the road, at that point of time.
The Tribunal has held that there was a breach of policy NC: 2025:KHC:10545 conditions and hence the owner of the bus alone is liabile to pay the compensation amount.
5. As a consequence, the owner has preferred M.F.A. No.8918/2015.
However, this appeal was dismissed for non-prosecution and after a period of 2921 days, the owner has filed an application for recalling this order.
6. The claimants are also before this Court seeking for enhancement of compensation by filing cross- objection in M.F.A. Crob.No.41/2024.

7. Having regard to the fact that the appeal was dismissed for non-prosecution, in my view, it would be appropriate to condone the delay in filing the application filed by the owner of the bus and also restore the appeal.

8. It is, however, made clear that the liability to pay interest on the compensation awarded shall lie only NC: 2025:KHC:10545 on the owner and not on the insurer in respect of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

9. As far as liability is concerned, it is settled law that if there is contention raised by the insurer that there was breach of policy, it would nevertheless have to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner of the bus.

In that view of the matter, the impugned order insofar as liability is concerned would have to be modified and have to be held that the owner of the bus would be liable to pay the compensation, but the insurer shall pay the same and thereafter proceed to recover the Sri Yellappa vs Smt Pramila on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184725824/
6 same from the owner of the bus.
10. As far as compensation is concerned, the deceased was aged about 31 years as on the date of the accident and there is no proof of actual income.

11. The Tribunal has recorded a finding that the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.5,000/- per NC:
2025:KHC:10545 month notionally since there was no evidence as to the actual income of the deceased.

In such circumstances, since the accident is of the year 2011, it would be appropriate to adopt the notional income determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which would be Rs.6,500/-.
Since the deceased was aged 31 years, future prospects of 40% requires to be added to the same, which makes his income to be Rs.9,100/- (Rs.6,500/- + Rs.2,600/-).

Since the deceased has 5 dependants, 1/4th requires to be deducted from the same, which makes his income to be Rs.6,825/- (Rs.9,100/- - Rs.2,275/-).
12.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.13,10,400/- (Rs.6,825/- X 12 X '16') towards 'loss of dependency'.
13.

The claimants would also be entitled to Rs.48,400/-
each towards 'loss of love and affection', which would be Rs.2,42,000/- (Rs.48,400/- X 5 members).

They - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC:10545 are also entitled to a sum of Rs.36,300/- towards 'miscellaneous expenses'.
14.
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.15,88,700/- as against Rs.7,56,000/- as compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the cross-objection.

15. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and thereafter shall recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.
16.
It is also made clear that in respect of the interest component on the amount awarded by the Tribunal.

it shall be the liability of the owner to pay the interest component, since he has chosen to file an appeal and had got the same dismissed for non- prosecution and is, therefore, responsible for the delay in the disposal of the appeal.
However, in respect of the enhanced compensation, the insurer will be liable to pay the interest.

Consequently, the appeal filed by the owner as well as the cross-objection filed by the victims are Sri Yellappa vs Smt Pramila on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184725824/
7 disposed of in the aforementioned terms.
18.
It is also made clear that the amount deposited by the owner of the bus shall be made over to the claimants.
19. The entire compensation amount shall be released to the claimants in the ratio of 60:10:10:10:10.
20. M.F.A. No.8918/2015 and M.F.A. Crob. No.41/2024 are, accordingly, disposed of.

21. Learned counsel for the appellant seeks to withdraw M.F.A. No.2445/2018, in the light of the fact that he has made an application for recalling the order dismissing the earlier appeal for non-prosecution.

22. The said submission is recorded.

In view of the dismissal of said appeal, I.A.
No.3/2018 for condonation of 1717 days' delay in filing the appeal does not survive for consideration.
24. In view of the disposal of the petition, all pending interlocutory applications, if any, stand disposed of.
